own_solution.law: Faraday's law and Ohm's law give Q = integral(I dt) = N A |ΔB| / R. Thus Q = 200 × π × (0.03 m)^2 × 0.080 T / (12 Ω).
assumptions: The coil remains stationary with its area perpendicular to the prescribed uniform field.
The stated resistance is constant and self-inductance is negligible.
An added series resistor contributes additional resistance to the original 12 Ω coil-and-wire circuit.
The independently powered doorbell has no specified coupling to the coil circuit.

TA07A.regime: The solenoid's uniform-field radius exceeds the coil radius of 3 cm, so the entire coil area remains threaded by the prescribed field.

TE656.regime: Treating the tube radius as the long solenoid's field radius, 7 cm exceeds the coil radius of 3 cm.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T676D and TD305 specify only a 'small resistor', whereas their corresponding quantified renderings TF32B and T451A specify 9.5 Ω, so the resistor variants do not preserve the required stated number and unit.

notes: The base physics is well-posed. With an additional 9.5 Ω series resistor, Q = 0.0144π/21.5 C. For either 85 ms sentence, I = N A ΔB/(R Δt), and multiplication by Δt cancels the duration. A resistor used only in an earlier run is disconnected from the present experiment in time. The invalid verdict concerns the packet's required numerical matching of variants; the unquantified disconnected resistors do not prevent calculation of the charge.
